exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Limit at Infinity of a Power Function With an Even Power

question.explanation:
The graph $y=x^{8}$ looks similar to an upward parabola, so \[ \lim_\limits{x \to -\infty} x^{8} = \infty. \]

Multiplication by the positive constant $5$ does not affect the limit at infinity. So, we have \begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \to -\infty} \left(5x^{8}\right) = \lim_\limits{x \to -\infty} \left(x^{8}\right) = \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{\infty}. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Limit at Infinity of a Power Function With an Even Power

question.explanation:
First, we divide the two functions, as follows: \begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \to \infty}\dfrac{p(x)}{q(x)} &=\lim_\limits{x \to \infty}\dfrac{\left(-2x^4\right)}{\left(-\dfrac{8}{x^6}\right)} \\[5pt] &=\lim_\limits{x \to \infty}\dfrac{x^{10}}{4}\\[5pt] &=\lim_\limits{x \to \infty}\left(\dfrac{1}{4} \cdot x^{10}\right)\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{4} \cdot \lim_\limits{x \to \infty}x^{10} \end{align*}

The graph $y=x^{10}$ looks similar to an upward parabola, so \[ \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} x^{10} = \infty . \]

Multiplication by the positive constant $\dfrac{1}{4}$ does not affect the limit at infinity So, we have \begin{align*} \dfrac{1}{4}\cdot \lim_\limits{x \to \infty}x^{10} = \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \left(x^{10}\right) = \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{\infty}. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Limit at Infinity of a Power Function With an Odd Power

question.explanation:
First, we calculate the powers and multiply the two functions, as follows:

\begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \left(p^3(x) \cdot q^2(x)\right) &=\lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \left(\left(p(x)\right)^3 \cdot \left(q(x)\right)^2\right)\\[5pt] &=\lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \left(\left(-3x^3\right)^3 \cdot \left(-3x^3\right)^2\right)\\[5pt] &=\lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \left(-27x^9 \cdot 9x^6\right)\\[5pt] &=\lim_\limits{x \to \infty}\left(\left(-27 \cdot 9 \right) x^{9+6} \right) \\[5pt] &=\lim_\limits{x \to \infty}\left(-243 \cdot x^{15} \right) \\[5pt] &=-243 \cdot \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} x^{15}\\ \end{align*}

The graph $y=x^{15}$ is power function with an odd positive power and therefore has the property that

\[ \lim_{x\to \infty } x^{15} = \infty. \]

Multiplication by the negative constant $-243$ changes the sign of the limit. So, we have

\begin{align*} &= -243\cdot\lim_\limits{x \to \infty} x^{15}\\[5pt] &=-\lim_\limits{x \to \infty} x^{15}\\[5pt] &= -\infty. \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that

\[ \lim_\limits{x \rightarrow \infty}\left( -243x^{15}\right) = -\infty. \]

example.title: Computing the Limit at Infinity of a Power Function With an Odd Power

question.explanation:
First, we multiply the two functions, as follows: \begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \to -\infty} \left(p(x) \cdot q(x)\right) &=\lim_\limits{x \to -\infty} \left(3x^2 \cdot 5x^7 \right)\\[5pt] &=\lim_\limits{x \to -\infty}\left(\left(3 \cdot 5 \right) x^{2+7} \right) \\[5pt] &=\lim_\limits{x \to -\infty}\left(15 \cdot x^{9} \right) \\[5pt] & = 15 \cdot \lim_\limits{x \to -\infty} x^{9} \end{align*}

The graph $y = x^{9}$ is power function with an odd positive power and therefore has the property that \[ \lim_{x \to -\infty} x^{9} = -\infty. \]

Multiplication by the positive constant $15$ does not affect the limit at infinity. So, we have \begin{align*} 15 \cdot \lim_\limits{x \to -\infty} x^{9} = \lim_\limits{x \to -\infty} x^{9} = -\infty. \end{align*}

Therefore, we conclude that \[ \lim_\limits{x \rightarrow -\infty}\left( 15x^{9}\right) = -\infty. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Limit at Infinity of a Constant Function

question.explanation:
First, let's calculate $x^2 \cdot q(x){:}$ \[ x^2 \cdot q(x) = x^2 \cdot \left( 15x^7 \right) = 15x^9 \]

When we divide the two functions $x^2 \cdot q(x)$ and $p(x),$ we get a constant, and the limit of a constant is just the constant itself: \begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \dfrac{x^2 \cdot q(x)}{p(x)} & = \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \dfrac{15x^9}{6x^9}\\[5pt] & = \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \dfrac{15}{6} \\[5pt] & = \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \dfrac{5}{2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5}{2} \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Limit at Infinity of a Constant Function

question.explanation:
First, let's calculate $x^2\cdot p(x){:}$ \[ x^2 \cdot p(x) = x^2 \cdot \left( -3x^5 \right) = -3x^7 \]

When we multiply the two functions $x^{2}\cdot p(x)$ and $q(x)$, we get a constant, and the limit of a constant is just the constant itself:

\begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \left(x^2\cdot p(x)\cdot q(x) \right) &=\lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \left(-3x^7 \cdot \dfrac{4}{x^{7}}\right) \\[5pt] &= \lim_\limits{x \to \infty} -12 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{-12} \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Limit at Infinity of a General Polynomial

question.explanation:
We identify the leading term and compute its limit:

\begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x \rightarrow \infty} ({\color{blue}4x^5}-7x^3+2x-9) &= \lim_\limits{x \rightarrow \infty} ({\color{blue}4x^5}) \\[3pt] &= 4 \cdot \lim_\limits{x \rightarrow \infty} (x^5) \\[3pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{\infty} \, . \end{align*}
